newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Fortis seals MeesPierson buy from ABN AMRO.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Fortis seals MeesPierson buy from ABN AMRO.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis said on Friday it had sealed the takeover of investment bank MeesPierson from Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV for 2.5 billion guilders ($1.43 billion).
It said the acquisition was expected to make a positive contribution to earnings per share from 1997 for both parent companies.

Fortis, jointly owned by Dutch group Fortis Amev and Belgian's Fortis AG, sees the purchase of MeesPierson as a significant step forward in its growth strategy, offering attractive opportunities in growth markets.
"After due diligence, further talks with the management of MeesPierson and the usual negotiations, agreement has now been reached on price and the other conditions," Fortis said.
"The price agreed for the acquisition is 2.5 billion guilders. The basis of the fixing of the price is the assets of the company at the end of 1996, including the results of 1996."
Fortis and ABN Amro signed a letter of intent for the deal on October 4.

Fortis said it expected to receive approval for the deal from the European Commission and other relevant authorities in the first quarter of 1997. MeesPierson would be incorporated in its results over 1997.
The purchase price was in line with analysts' expectations at the time it was first agreed.

MeesPierson, created through the April 1993 merger of Mees & Hope with Pierson, Heldring and Pierson, has about 4,000 staff around the world, including Europe, the Far East and United States, and more than 50 billion guilders of assets under management.
It made an operating profit of 182 million guilders and a net profit of 250 million guilders in 1995.
The sale ends an overlap of activities within ABN AMRO, which has expanded into investment banking in recent years, bringing these new operations into competition with MeesPierson itself.
Fortis AMEV shares were 60 cents higher at 55.40 guilders by 0955 GMT, while ABN AMRO was up 2.40 at 111.30.
